svg.title: Six waiting rooms between load and capacity
svg.desc: A sixty-second timeline where load steps from 10 to 200 requests per second at zero, followed by six hachured waiting-room blocks laid end to end - metrics staleness 12.5 seconds, HPA sync 7.5, scheduling 0.3, container start and warm-up 3.3, readiness probe 2.5 and endpoint propagation 1.2 - bracketed as a predicted median of 27.3 seconds against a measured 31, with a dashed cold-image-pull block adding fourteen, a p99 latency curve spiking and only recovering at the end, a CPU quota bar half filled and half marked THROTTLED, and a comparison showing in-flight requests leading CPU utilisation.
svg.text: Six waiting rooms between load and capacity
worst case, every maximum at once: 53.7 s
31 seconds of degraded service that autoscaling cannot prevent
the HPA does not make you fast. It makes you cheap. If
your spike is shorter than 31 s, autoscaling is not the
7 image pull 0 s cached / 14 s cold
the one that ruins your day
and the throttle you did not ask for
4 threads burn the 100 ms quota in 12.5 ms, then stall for
...and if a whole NODE has to be created first? -> +60 to 180 s
